land.text: the Aksumite heartland, Tigray and the Eritrean highlands, conquered 'around 960' by Gudit, who 'ruled over what remained of the kingdom' for 40 years before 'the last of her dynasty was overthrown by Mara Takla Haymanot in 1137'

predecessors.note: Not at birth: Cliopatria's Zagwe row begins in 947 on Lasta alone (outside the Aksum shape); the heartland comes in 960 (ledger, confidence 1). Infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Aksum'.

land.text: the whole kingdom: Lasta, Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara to Lake Tana

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Ethiopian Empire'. Yekuno Amlak's reign began 10 August 1270 (Yekuno Amlak page); Cliopatria keeps the Zagwe to 1271 and starts the Ethiopian Empire in 1272. The ethiopian-empire dossier (af-01-b/c) should start in 1270.

capitals.name: Adefa (Roha, Lalibela)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Adefa', the old name of Lalibela (Roha), without years; 'In the late 12th century, Lalibela's knowledge of Jerusalem inspired the expansion of his capital'. Coordinates from the project gazetteer (places.jsonl 'Lalibela'). Before 1137 the seat of Gudit's line is unknown and the dot stays here.

correction.text: Lasta as drawn (14,454 km2 around Lalibela, 'the power base of Mara, who was born there') from 947; the Aksumite heartland (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Axum shape of 946) from c. 960, when 'Queen Gudit destroyed the remnants of the Kingdom of Aksum' (ledger); the Zagwe proper from 1137 ('Established: 1137'; 'Other theories for the start: c. 930')

keyframe_review.note: 947-1138: Cliopatria's 947 start is the page's 'other theories' (c. 930; Conti Rossini's list c. 916-1270, the long list c. 937-1270; the Dabra Ferem and Hasani Dan'el inscriptions 'likely in the early 10th century'), not its 1137 establishment. The 947-1136 years are Gudit's line and the Aksumite remnant, folded into this dossier for want of a Cliopatria row (confidence 1). The infobox gives no area figure; 14,454 km2 is Lasta only. Repair pass: the spec is the shape at 947 (Lasta); before the repair it gave the Zagwe Tigray and all Eritrea from 947, 62,213 km2 of which Kingdom of Axum still held until 960.

correction.text: Lasta with the lands Buxton assigns to direct Zagwe rule: 'probably embraced the highlands of modern Eritrea, Tigray, Wag and Bete Amhara and thence westwards towards Lake Tana' (Lake Tana in Begemder)

keyframe_review.note: 1139-1259: the Cliopatria shape is Lasta alone, a fraction of the kingdom the page describes; Tigray (with Eritrea) and the Amhara region (Wag, Bete Amhara, Begemder) are added. No border move is dated in these years; 'The only regular relations seem to have been maintained with Egypt and Jerusalem'. The Red Sea coast and Shewa are not mentioned on the page. Repair pass: the Kingdom of Axum 946 shape (the 960 gain) is added to the union so that keyframe and ledger agree: it holds 131 cells (about 33,000 km2, mostly Afar) outside Tigray (region).

correction.text: the same extent (Lasta, Tigray and the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara to Lake Tana), ending in 1270 rather than 1271: 'Yekuno Amlak pursued the last Zagwe king and killed him at the Battle of Ansata in 1270'

keyframe_review.note: 1260-1271: Cliopatria keeps the row to 1271 and starts the Ethiopian Empire in 1272; Yekuno Amlak reigned from 10 August 1270.

region.text: Lasta, 'the power base of Mara, who was born there'

ledger.note: 947: a kingdom in Lasta, by the early tradition. The page: 'Established: 1137' with 'Other theories for the start: c. 930'; Conti Rossini's king list spans c. 916-1270 and the long list c. 937-1270; three inscriptions at Axum naming Dabra Ferem and Hasani Dan'el are 'likely in the early 10th century'. The year is Cliopatria's; Lasta lies outside Cliopatria's Aksum shape, so the land is taken from nobody. Repair pass: the Mara Takla Haymanot page has only 'claims that this dynasty started around 1137' (and an infobox reign of 960-970), so 947 stays Cliopatria's year at confidence 1.

region.text: the land Aksum dissolves in 960 (Tigray and the Eritrean highlands as Cliopatria draws them): 'According to one tradition, around 960, Queen Gudit destroyed the remnants of the Kingdom of Aksum'

ledger.note: c. 960: Gudit destroys Aksum; the highlands pass to the line the Zagwe succeed. The Zagwe page: 'According to one tradition, around 960, Queen Gudit destroyed the remnants of the Kingdom of Aksum' and 'For 40 years she ruled over what remained of the kingdom, eventually passing on the throne to her descendants, with Mara marrying the daughter of the last king of Aksum, Dil Na'od'; 'the last of her dynasty was overthrown by Mara Takla Haymanot in 1137'. James Bruce makes Mara 'a cousin of Gudit who succeeded her' (Gudit page). The land is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Axum shape of 946 (96,102 km2), exactly what the kingdom-of-axum dossier hands over in 960; the earlier 'Tigray (region)' (171,787 km2, Tigray plus all Eritrea) took 109,549 km2 that Aksum never held, and Aksum had lost the northern Eritrean plateau to the Beja c. 700 (kingdom-of-axum ledger), so the plateau part of the shape is Aksum's by Cliopatria's drawing only. Folded into this dossier because Cliopatria has no Gudit row. Repair pass, thin item: the Gudit page gives 'ca. 960', 'reigned for 40 years', Aksum 'and its countryside' laid waste and Damo 'in Tigray'; it names no land of her own, so a 'gudit' dossier would still lack territory.

1137: Mara Takla Haymanot founds the Zagwe dynasty (infobox 'Established: 1137'; the Zagwe 'ruled large parts of the territory from approximately 1137 to 1270 AD'). Per tradition he overthrew the last of Gudit's line, or was 'a general of Dil Na'od and overthrew his father-in-law'. Same state in this dossier since Cliopatria's row begins in 947; colour continues (rule 2).

region.text: the Zagwe kingdom at the extent Buxton describes beyond Lasta and the Aksumite heartland: 'probably embraced the highlands of modern Eritrea, Tigray, Wag and Bete Amhara and thence westwards towards Lake Tana (Begemder)'

ledger.note: 1137: the Zagwe kingdom at the extent Buxton describes. The page does not date the acquisition of Wag, Bete Amhara and Begemder; the dynasty's establishment year is used and the land taken from nobody (no Cliopatria row covers it). Repair pass: the region adds the Tigray (region) land outside the Kingdom of Axum 946 shape (the highlands of modern Eritrea of Buxton's sentence), so that the 1139 keyframe has an event behind every cell; the Aksumite heartland itself came in 960. The Lalibela page (read as Gebre Mesqel Lalibela, 'reigning from 1181 to 1221') gives no conquest or extent, and the Mara Takla Haymanot page has only 'embracing parts of Lasta, Wag, Tigray, and perhaps northern Begemder', so the acquisition stays undated at confidence 1.

region.text: the kingdom: Lasta, Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara to Lake Tana

ledger.note: 1270: Yekuno Amlak kills the last Zagwe king at Ansata. 'Yekuno Amlak pursued the last Zagwe king and killed him at the Battle of Ansata in 1270'; his reign began 10 August 1270 (Yekuno Amlak page, which gives no year for the battle); the last king is named Za-Ilmaknun, 'a pseudonym' (Taddesse Tamrat: Yetbarak; Getachew Mekonnen Hasen: Na'akueto La'ab). Yekuno Amlak 'received considerable aid from the Muslim Sultanate of Shewa'. The ethiopian-empire dossier should begin in 1270 (Cliopatria 1272).

wars.name: Yekuno Amlak's revolt and the Battle of Ansata
wars.outcome: Yekuno Amlak, escaped from imprisonment on Mount Malot and backed by 'the Amhara provinces and Shewa' and 'considerable aid from the Muslim Sultanate of Shewa', killed the last Zagwe king at Ansata in 1270 and founded the Solomonic dynasty (reign from 10 August 1270).
wars.note: The revolt's start is undated on both pages; only the battle year is given. The Zagwe 'fell victim to Jewish raids' and had been defeated by Damot after Zena Petros's failed tribute campaign (undated), so no war entry is made for those.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the extent is Buxton's 'probably embraced ...' and the Cliopatria shape; the Shewan, Damot and coastal frontiers are unknown.

notes:
Start. Cliopatria runs the Zagwe from 947; the page establishes the dynasty in 1137 with 'other theories' of c. 930 and king lists from c. 916 or c. 937. This dossier keeps 947 (confidence 1) so that the Aksumite heartland has an owner after Aksum's 960 collapse: Gudit's line (c. 960-1000) and the interregnum to 1137 are folded in, with a rename event at 1137 for the Zagwe proper. A gap-filler may split a 'gudit' state (960-c. 1000) if a page gives it territory; the three king lists on the page contradict each other (5, 11 or 16 names), so the rulers key is omitted.

Extent. Cliopatria's three shapes are Lasta alone (14,454 km2); Buxton's description adds Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag, Bete Amhara and the land to Lake Tana, given here as the gazetteer's 'Tigray (region)' (Tigray plus all Eritrea) and the Amhara region, both wider than the page's words (the Red Sea coast and Shewa are not mentioned). The Sultanate of Shewa (slug sultanate-of-shewa, Cliopatria lacks it; conquered by Yekuno Amlak in 1285) and the Kingdom of Damot (kingdom-of-damot; 'the pre-eminent power in the region', which defeated the Zagwe at an undated time) need dossiers from af-01-x or the Ifat/Adal part.

End. 1270 (Battle of Ansata; Yekuno Amlak's reign from 10 August 1270), against Cliopatria's 1271/1272 hand-over; the ethiopian-empire dossier should start in 1270. The Zagwe remnant in Lasta (the Wagshum line) is not on the pages opened.

Repair of 2026-10-18 (reviewer): zagwe-dynasty_947 is now the shape at 947 (Lasta), the Aksumite heartland coming in 960 as a ledger event; the 960 gain is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Axum 946 shape (what the kingdom-of-axum dossier hands over) instead of Tigray (region), and the misquoted 'her line ruled for about 40 years' is replaced by the page's 'For 40 years she ruled over what remained of the kingdom' (also in the predecessor note); the 1137 gain now adds the Tigray (region) land outside the Axum shape, and the 1139 and 1260 keyframes and the dissolve region carry the Axum shape, so that keyframes and ledger agree (the 1139 shape is about 361,000 km2 against Cliopatria's 14,454 km2 for Lasta, a ratio of 25, the same acknowledgement as before: Buxton's description, regions wider than the page). Pages tried for the thin items: Mara Takla Haymanot and Gudit (no new dates), Lalibela (reign 1181-1221, no extent; 'Lalibela_(king)' did not load, 'Gebre_Mesqel_Lalibela' did).
